name: Daptomycin
route_note: Once-daily IV injection or infusion; doses are weight-based.
originator: Eli Lilly and Company; developed by Cubist Pharmaceuticals

discovery.note: Isolated from Streptomyces roseosporus from a soil sample from Mount Ararat, Turkey; Lilly halted development because of muscle toxicity.

tagline: Membrane-active lipopeptide for MRSA bacteraemia and right-sided endocarditis
summary: Daptomycin is a cyclic lipopeptide that rapidly kills Gram-positive bacteria, including MRSA and vancomycin-resistant enterococci, by disrupting the cell membrane. It is used for complicated skin infections and S. aureus bacteraemia, but not for pneumonia because lung surfactant inactivates it.
mechanism: In the presence of calcium, daptomycin inserts its lipid tail into the cytoplasmic membrane of Gram-positive bacteria, oligomerises and clusters in fluid, phosphatidylglycerol-rich regions. This displaces membrane-bound cell-wall synthesis enzymes, causes depolarisation and potassium efflux, and leads to rapid cell death without lysis.

It cannot cross the Gram-negative outer membrane. Pulmonary surfactant sequesters daptomycin, explaining its failure in community-acquired pneumonia trials. Reduced susceptibility arises through mprF and other membrane-charge mutations.
uses: Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia, including right-sided endocarditis
Off-label: vancomycin-resistant enterococcal infections, osteomyelitis and prosthetic infections

history.title: Licensing
history.detail: Cubist Pharmaceuticals licenses daptomycin from Eli Lilly and redesigns once-daily dosing to reduce muscle toxicity.

history.title: US approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Cubicin for complicated skin and skin-structure infections.

history.title: Bacteraemia indication
history.detail: Approval is extended to S. aureus bloodstream infections, including right-sided endocarditis.

history.title: Eosinophilic pneumonia warning
history.detail: The FDA warns of eosinophilic pneumonia associated with daptomycin.

serious: Myopathy and rhabdomyolysis (risk higher with statins)

facts: Weekly creatine phosphokinase monitoring is recommended during daptomycin therapy.
Daptomycin was originally found in a soil sample from Mount Ararat.
